assets.name_fr: Air Exchange — concept du réacteur, publication Raising the Bar 2004
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one opaque panoramic 2D fighting-background candidate, archival concept adaptation, not an animation or separated parallax layers.
Primary request: Translate ONLY the supplied Viktor Antonov Air Exchange reactor concept reproduced as Airex_reactor.jpg from Half-Life 2: Raising the Bar, publication version 2004, into a detailed wide side-view game background. The creation date and hidden geometry of the original concept remain unknown. Do not merge the 2002 development maps, leaked builds, fan recreations, or retail Citadel into this design.
Reference image role: the supplied single archival concept is the sole architecture, material, lighting and palette reference.
Composition: a wide continuous panorama, approximately 16:9, side-on readable for a 2D fight. Keep the massive tall rust-brown cylindrical reactor rising in the center-right, its broad tapering buttresses and sloped support legs, dense low blocky dark industrial buildings behind it, and tiny sparse cyan-green window lights. Preserve the murky brown and charcoal atmosphere, ochre glow through heavy polluted clouds at the far left, and the dominant looming silhouette. Preserve the isolated single concept's design and do not introduce additional major towers or invented machinery.
The lower fifth is a continuous simple industrial stone/concrete floor crossing the full width at one level, with the walkable baseline at about 79 percent image height. This modest level strip is the explicit functional 2D adaptation, not a claim that the source depicts a playable map. Keep large structures behind the fight plane; no fence across the foreground, no jumping platforms, no stair steps, no gaps. Retain the dark archival mood while making large shapes legible.
Style: detailed hand-painted game background, crisp structural silhouette, restrained material textures faithful to the limited source rather than adding ornate fantasy detail.
No people, enemies, vehicles, weapons, HUD, words, captions, logos, watermarks, borders, comparison panels or contact sheet. Deliver one complete original opaque panorama.

assets.reference_scope: One translucent volume pose study, anchored by the full-body grate capture and near view of envelope/interior. Both show the same industrial demo setting, not SDK npc_blob/headcrab or Portal gels. No animation, grille passage or consumption sequence is validated.
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one isolated translucent archival creature sprite on a real transparent background.
Primary request: Create a single still 2D game-art study of the Blob volume from the Episode Three experimental footage in Valve's Half-Life 2 20th Anniversary Documentary, using ONLY the two supplied documentary frames. This is an archival candidate pose, not a certified official sprite or complete animation.
Reference roles: image 1 shows the complete rounded translucent envelope in the industrial grate scene; use its silhouette and material as the primary reference. Image 2 is a nearer view of the same demonstrated creature, used only for the limited visible dark/red interior and warm translucent skin. Do not copy any background object through the body.
One whole solitary near-round irregular ovoid gelatinous volume, resting with a softly compressed lower curve, almost spherical but subtly sagging. Silhouette large and completely contained with generous transparent margins, camera approximately level with its middle for side-view readability. Preserve a clear amber-beige translucent envelope with subtle cool tones and small soft wet highlights, not an opaque stone or shiny hard glass sphere. Through the body show only the subdued dark and muted reddish diffuse internal shapes and fine branching structures visible in the reference. Keep uncertain internal detail indistinct; do not invent anatomy, a mouth, face, eyes, teeth, organs or expressive features. Preserve gentle irregularity of the envelope, no rigid segmentation, no limbs or extra tentacles outside it.
Use a genuine alpha channel: the body itself must remain partly transparent while visible inner shapes and rim highlights provide readability on both black and white. Background fully transparent, not a checkerboard painting. Do not retain any floor, grating, planks, barrels, held weapon, reticle, yellow HUD or text from the references. No shadow rectangle or decorative glow. No Headcrab, Snark, humanoid, Portal gel or SDK test-model substitution. assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one isolated archival ice-effect sprite with a real transparent background.
Primary request: A single static irregular mass of pale translucent ice as shown in the supplied Episode Three Ice Gun experimental footage from Valve's Half-Life 2 20th Anniversary Documentary. Depict the observed ice formation only, not a weapon, a beam, a shot or an entire environment.
Reference roles: image 1 is the main source for the lumpy joined ice wall/ledge and frosted material. Image 2 provides a second close view of the same test effect's surface, to confirm its milky cyan transparency and irregular rounded contour. These are grey prototype test scenes; do not import the separate painted Arctic concept into this effect.
Compose one compact connected uneven ice mass in a clear side view with a shallow view of its top, broad enough to read as a low obstacle, a visibly flat grounded lower edge, rising and sloping unevenly with soft fractured edges. Preserve pale icy blue translucent material with milky white frost patches, thin cracks and restrained wet glints. The silhouette should be made of joined rough rounded ice chunks as in the test, not a collection of tall pointed crystal needles, a magic shield or decorative fantasy gems. Keep the object fully in frame with generous transparent margins and no arbitrary platform or surrounding snow floor.
The output has real alpha outside the object and natural partial transparency within its clear parts. No solid white background and no painted checkerboard. Remove all context from the new sprite: no gun or hands, no laser, no smoke trail, no buildings, soldiers, stairs, railings, HUD, text, logos, watermark, panels or animation sheet. Do not invent an official final Ice Gun model. This is one archival still-effect study, with no animation, collision or game timing implied.
